Kimberly — quick summary from my scan.

- Usage: Spinnered bursts from two IP ranges over the past 48 hours; total tokens consumed by the Nimbus org are 1.2M in 7 days (see attached CSV snippet).
- Accounts: We see three active sub-accounts under the Nimbus org. Two of them were created within the last 10 days and are tied to similar email domains (dev-*).
- Patterns: Repeated credit requests in the last 30 days — two support threads with different contacts asking for more credits (HubSpot HS-1789, HS-1792).

I attached audit-logs-snip.txt and the usage CSV. My recommendation: hold on provisioning the full 500k until we confirm whether these are legitimate parallel teams for the same company or a coordinated multi-account attempt to amplify free credits.

If Kimberly still wants to move quickly for the pilot, we can provision 100k now and re-evaluate after a short canary period (24–48 hrs). Jordan, can ops pull a fuller IP/device correlation and any unusual onboarding automation traces?

—Ben

On Tue, Jun 29, 2027 at 09:18, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> I attached audit-logs-snip.txt and the usage CSV. My recommendation: hold on provisioning the full 500k until we confirm whether these are legitimate parallel teams for the same company or a coordinated multi-account attempt to amplify free credits.

I pulled deeper traces. Highlights:
- The two recently created sub-accounts show near-identical user-agent strings and identical first-request timestamps (within 2s).
- Payment info: none present (still in trial), IPs map to a cloud provider region that is different from Nimbus corporate IP ranges.
- No SSO link observed; onboarding appears email-based for those sub-accounts.

This looks suspicious for automated account creation used to farm multiple eval grants. I recommend we: 1) deny the 500k top-up for now; 2) offer a single 100k top-up to the main org account contingent on a short verification call and a signed pilot scoping note; 3) open a fraud review ticket and flag these sub-accounts for manual verification.

I can open INFRA-9843 and add device/IP correlation output there.

—Jordan
